Ezekiel 20:1 is a new episode, in the seventh year, in which elders come to enquire of the LORD
Ezekiel 20:45 begins another word of the LORD immediately after the prophecy to the elders
Ezekiel 21 continues the judgment from the fire of 20:45-48 with the image of the LORD's sword
Ezekiel 22:2 charges the bloody city, continuing the judgment of chapter 21
Ezekiel 23 uses a similar picture of unfaithful women as chapter 16 for Jerusalem and Samaria
Ezekiel 23 follows chapter 22 in the series of words against Jerusalem
Ezekiel 24:2 dates the word to the day Babylon set himself against Jerusalem, the siege the preceding chapters announce
Ezekiel 25 follows the announcement of Jerusalem's fall and the sanctuary's profaning in chapter 24, which the nations mocked
Ezekiel 26 continues the oracles against nations that mocked Jerusalem, begun in chapter 25
Ezekiel 27 is a lamentation for the city whose fall is announced in chapter 26
Ezekiel 28 turns from the city of Tyre in 26-27 to her ruler
Ezekiel 28:20 gives the next word of the LORD in the oracle series on Tyre and Zidon
Ezekiel 29:1 begins the oracles against Egypt after those against the other neighbours in chapters 25-28
Ezekiel 30 continues the oracles against Egypt from chapter 29
Ezekiel 31 is a further oracle against Pharaoh and Egypt, dated to the eleventh year (31:1)
Ezekiel 32 continues the oracles against Egypt and its Pharaoh in the twelfth year
Ezekiel 33:7-9 restates the watchman charge first given in 3:17-19
Ezekiel 33 returns to Israel after the oracles against the nations in chapters 25-32
Ezekiel 33:22 says the LORD opened his mouth, fulfilling the dumbness announced in 3:26-27 and 24:27
Ezekiel 34 follows the report of the fall of Jerusalem with a word to the shepherds of Israel
Ezekiel 35 is the next word, setting the judgment on Seir before the restoration of Israel's mountains in 36
Ezekiel 36:5 and 36:1-4 answer the claims against the land that the previous chapter attributes to Seir
Ezekiel 36:1 speaks to the mountains of Israel, as chapter 6 did in judgment
Ezekiel 36:16 continues the word to the house of Israel about the land and the return begun in 36:1-15
Ezekiel 37:14 promises the LORD's Spirit in them and their placement in their own land, as in 36:27-28
Ezekiel 37:15 continues in the same chapter as the bones, which the LORD calls the whole house of Israel (37:11), uniting Judah and Joseph
Ezekiel 38:8 speaks of a land brought back from the sword and gathered out of many people, following the restoration promises of chapters 36-37
Ezekiel 39:1 continues the prophecy against Gog begun in chapter 38
Ezekiel 40:1 begins a new vision in the twenty-fifth year of captivity after the oracles of chapters 33-39
Ezekiel 41:1 begins with the man bringing Ezekiel to the temple after the measuring of the courts in chapter 40
Ezekiel 43:1 follows the measuring of the temple in 40-42
Ezekiel 43:3 refers to the vision seen when Ezekiel came to destroy the city and by the Chebar, and the glory comes back by the east gate toward which it departed (10:18, 11:23)
Ezekiel 44:4 sees the glory of the LORD filling the house, as in 43:5
Ezekiel 45 continues the instructions for the sanctuary, the priests and the prince given in chapters 43-44
Ezekiel 46 continues the regulations for the prince and offerings of chapter 45
Ezekiel 47:1 brings Ezekiel back to the door of the house, after the tour of its kitchens and courts in 46:19-24
Ezekiel 47:13 follows the vision of the river with the borders for the inheritance
Ezekiel 48 gives the tribal portions within the borders set out in 47:13-23
Daniel 1:1-2 and Jeremiah 25:1, 9-11 both describe Nebuchadnezzar's power over Judah in the days of Jehoiakim
Daniel 1:1-7 introduces the setting that the book overview describes
Daniel 2:13-18 involves Daniel and his three companions, introduced in chapter 1, and Nebuchadnezzar's wise men
Daniel 3:12 says Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were set over the province of Babylon, as stated in 2:49
Daniel 4 is the same king's testimony to the signs and wonders of the high God (4:2-3), following those in chapters 2-3
Daniel 5:18-22 recounts the humbling of Nebuchadnezzar told in chapter 4 as the reason Belshazzar should have humbled himself
Daniel 5:31 says Darius the Median took the kingdom, and chapter 6 begins in Darius's reign
Daniel 7:1 dates the vision to the first year of Belshazzar, an earlier date than chapter 6, but the book now moves from narratives to visions
Daniel 7:15-16 begins when Daniel asks one standing by the meaning of the vision in 7:1-14
Daniel 8:1 says the vision came after the one that appeared at the first, in chapter 7
Daniel 9:2 says Daniel understood from the books the seventy years of Jerusalem's desolation that the word of the LORD gave to Jeremiah (Jeremiah 25:11-12)
Daniel 9:1 is dated to the first year of Darius, later than the vision of chapter 8 in the third year of Belshazzar
Daniel 9:20-23 describes Gabriel coming while Daniel was still praying the prayer in 9:3-19
Daniel 10:1 gives a further revelation to Daniel, later, in the third year of Cyrus
Daniel 11:1-2 continues the speech of the messenger who in 10:14 said he came to make Daniel understand what will befall his people in the latter days
Daniel 11:21 continues the list of kings begun in 11:2-20
Daniel 12:1 begins "at that time" and continues the revelation of chapters 10-11
